title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_334.txt
concise_summary: PKD synthesizes Malebranche's occasionalism and Platonic Forms theory to rationalize his 2-3-74 mystical experience, arguing that reality is a unified field in which God operates as the sole active principle, that we perceive intelligible archetypes rather than material objects, and that divine presence can manifest spatiotemporally through 'wormhole' reconstitution of Christ-as-map, explaining his simultaneous experience of being both in 1974 USA and 35 CE Jerusalem.
key_claims: The apparent reality of world and apparent non-existence of God actually proves God's power, because only divine power can sustain such convincing illusion (occasionalism refutes naive empiricism)
We never perceive physical objects directly; we perceive intelligible archetypal ideas in God's mind (vision in God), making Spinoza's pantheism false and Malebranche's system correct
Multiple discrete entities and causation are illusory; reality is one integrated coherent field unified by God's sole volition acting through it as transducer/medium

The intelligible archetypal eidos (Christ as the divine self-map) can distribute itself across any spacetime via 'wormhole' constitution, collapsing space, time, causation, and self into mystical simultaneity
2-3-74 was not hallucination but direct apperception of the Mens Dei (divine mind) which is God's self-aware knowledge, triggering retrieval across human consciousness as mode locus
recurring_concepts: Malebranche's occasionalism (God as sole cause, bodies as occasions without real causal power)
Vision in God (directly perceiving divine mind's intelligible archetypes, not material world)
Meta-abstraction (access to universal essences above empirical perception)
Set/ground discrimination and feature-extraction (perceptual mechanisms revealing divine masquerade)
Cosmic transubstantiation (divine entering reality field from outside, camouflaged as ordinary causal process)
Acosmic Panentheism (God beyond but acting through unified field, not identical to it)
Eidos/intelligible archetypes (Platonic forms in God's mind underlying apparent multiplicity)
Mens Dei (the mind of God as unified singular consciousness containing self-map of itself as Christ)
people_entities: Philip K. Dick (PKD, author of the Exegesis)
Nicolas Malebranche (17th century philosopher whose occasionalism PKD claims explains 2-3-74)
Plato (ancient philosopher whose theory of Forms PKD invokes as metaphysical framework)
Baruch Spinoza (contemporary of Malebranche; PKD rejects his pantheism as inconsistent with empirical data)
Gottfried Leibniz (contemporary of Malebranche; PKD mentions his preestablished harmony)
Benedict Spinoza (philosophy of unified field rejected in favor of Malebranche)
St. Paul/St. Paul (early Christian cosmologist whose mysticism PKD invokes to explain Christian rather than merely theistic elements)
Augustine (Christian theologian; source of Malebranche's theology)
James Stephens (referenced: 'Set it spinning' quote about God sustaining reality)
John Varley (science fiction author; story 'Overdrawn at the Memory Bank' cited for mimesis/feature-extraction concept)
Thomas (apostle; PKD experienced simultaneous identity as Thomas at Last Supper and as PKD in 1974)
Christ (the Logos, divine self-map, intelligible eidos incarnate, retrieved through proper eidos in human consciousness)
texts_works: Ubik (PKD's novel, expressions of divine being through ordinary objects and processes)
Maze of Death (PKD's novel, exemplifying feature-extraction and mimesis)
Overdrawn at the Memory Bank (John Varley story, cited as analogue to feature-extraction)
Plato's Theory of Forms (Platonic metaphysics foundational to the argument)
Malebranche's occasionalism (metaphysical system foundational to argument)
autobiographical: 2-3-74 mystical experience: apperception of God's power demonstrated via revelation of world's unreality and mechanism of illusion (described as 'milestone in my thinking')
Acquired in 3-74 perfect a priori knowledge of world over and above empirical knowledge
Saw 'King Felix cypher' (instance of set/ground discrimination revealing divine presence)
Letters to Pat discussing apperception of mind attribute of substantia blended with empirical spatial extension attribute
Experienced visions like holograms: mailman, bus, palm trees—external events apprehended as intelligible archetypes
Last October (autumn 1977) realized meta-abstraction pointed to common essence via Platonic eidos
Last night (before this entry) realized simultaneity: experiencing both USA 1974 and Rome AD 45 at once, simultaneously Thomas and PKD
Identification of VALIS as God or Cosmic Christ
Awareness of God's continual sustaining of reality (not merely initial creation)
Recognition of divine machinery operating and salvation as rescue from mundane trap
theological_motifs: Fall (Gnosticism; loss of awareness of true reality)
Gnosticism (occlusion vs. salvation; unknowing control by adversarial situation)
Salvation and rescue (supernatural intervention breaking mundane control)
The Last Supper (spatial-temporal set in which divine was mapped; retrievable mystically)
Jerusalem 35 CE (historical locus of divine incarnation, eternally present via eidos)
Divine incarnation: Word made flesh (Christ as intelligible eidos mapped once spatiotemporally, retrievable eternally)
Mystical union with God (annihilation of space, time, causation, self)
Cosmic Christ (theophany; Christ as self-map of Mens Dei)
Panentheism (God beyond but acting through field, acosmic form)
Divine camouflage in world (not pantheism but God masquerading as natural process)
Sophia/Wisdom traditions (implicit in Pan-Indian thought synthesis)
literary_self_ref: Ubik as expression of 'This is all in God' and vision in God (divine presence posing as ordinary causal process)
Maze of Death exemplifying feature-extraction and mimesis—divine disguised as maze/trap
Overdrawn at the Memory Bank (Varley) as analogue to PKD's own cosmological mimicry concept
King Felix cypher as lived instance of set/ground discrimination in PKD's own perceptual field (mimicry/extraction theme)
Letters to Pat as earlier formulation of a priori knowledge now ratified by Malebranche
symbols_images: The 'Black Iron Prison' (implicit: the world as trap, occlusion from salvation, control by invincibly impinging stimuli)
Set/ground discrimination (visual metaphor for revealing hidden divine presence beneath apparent causal surface)
Hologram (the visions—mailman, bus, palm trees—as multidimensional images of single eidos distributed across perception)
King Felix cypher (instance of divine sign hidden in ordinary perception)
Wormhole constitution (spatial metaphor for timeless distribution of Christ-eidos across multiple spatiotemporal locales)
Transducer/medium (God as signal transmitted through reality-field like electrical current through conducting medium)
Map within map (Mens Dei containing self-map of itself as intelligible eidos of Christ)
The wise horn (Christ as mediator in adversarial situation)
The surd (the inexplicable perturbation of 2-3-74, now made rational by Malebranche's framework)
Mode locus (human consciousness as receptacle/locus through which divine self-maps retrieve themselves)
tensions: God + world are NOT the same (rejecting pantheism) BUT God is camouflaged in world (seeming to require pantheistic language)—resolved by distinction between creation + causation, God's external perturbation

Spinoza's contemporaries Leibniz and Spinoza both posit unified field, but Malebranche differs from Spinoza in distinguishing God from field (PKD does not fully explain why Leibniz's preestablished harmony would differ)
We are simultaneously 'not here, not now' AND localized in specific spatiotemporal bodies—PKD notes this paradox but only partially resolves it through eidos distribution
Divine transcendence (God beyond reality-field) vs. divine immanence (God acting through it as sole power)—PKD invokes 'acosmic Panentheism' but the spatial metaphors break down
Malebranche's theological occasionalism (salvation doctrine) vs. PKD's cosmological use (metaphysical framework for explaining mystical simultaneity)—utility vs. fidelity unclear
The entry truncates mid-sentence, leaving unresolved the mechanism by which human mode locus 'suddenly' gains capacity for divine consciousness-sharing
